title: Memory Manager domain configuration
description: What a consuming domain may configure. Validated at startup; the service refuses to start on invalid configuration rather than degrading to a default. Keys that could switch off a security rule deliberately do not exist.

name.description: Neutral domain identifier, used as a resource prefix and as a metric label.

retention.description: ONE period for the whole domain. Per-topic retention is not possible: TTL is a bank-level setting and each domain has one bank (verified 2026-10-22). Applied by platform Terraform; declared here so the service can report what it believes is in force.

topics.description: The domain's topic vocabulary. A topic absent from this list is unknown and is rejected.

classification.description: Only non-sensitive topics are eligible for storage. Sensitive and restricted are excluded — not a permissions question, the domain stores nothing in them.

allowInferred.description: Whether a fact with basis 'inferred' may be stored. Defaults to false, so an unsupported inference is rejected unless the domain opts in.

callers.description: Registered agents and what each may do. A caller absent from this list is not registered and is refused.

subject.description: The service account or token subject this caller presents.

operations.description: A caller granted only 'recall' can never write.

topics.description: Topic ids this caller may use. Must exist in 'topics'.

identity.description: How an end-user token is verified. The subject resolves to a scope server-side.

extensions.description: Module paths for the domain's implementations. An omitted entry uses the platform default; security-relevant defaults fail closed, so omitting pii-classifier or policy-provider means nothing is stored.

quota.description: This domain's allocated share of the SHARED project Memory Bank quota, divided across instances at startup. The service refuses to start without it.

logLevel.description: DEBUG does not enable payload logging. The prohibited-field list in security rule S-4 is absolute at every level.

idempotency.description: The per-instance replay cache behind the Idempotency-Key contract. Both bounds have defaults, so a domain that configures nothing still gets the behaviour. The guarantee holds within one instance; across instances it rests on session affinity and provider consolidation.

retentionSeconds.description: How long a key is remembered. Longer than any plausible client retry budget, short enough to bound memory. A cached response also makes a policy change invisible for this long: a fact refused under a tightened classifier still replays its earlier result until the entry expires.

maxEntries.description: A hard ceiling independent of expiry. Needed because a burst of unique keys arrives faster than anything ages out.
